undergraduate_aid_policy.policy_summary: MIT is need-blind for undergraduate applicants worldwide and meets 100% of demonstrated financial need without loans. For families with typical assets, MIT states that income below $200,000 qualifies for full tuition coverage and income below $100,000 for a $0 expected parent contribution. A $0 parent contribution does not mean that students have no costs or responsibilities.

description: Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) is the world's preeminent private research institution in science, engineering, and technology. Located on 168 acres along the Charles River in Cambridge, Massachusetts, MIT combines an undergraduate college of ~4,500 students with a powerhouse graduate research body of ~7,350 students across five schools and the Stephen A. Schwarzman College of Computing. MIT operates a fully need-blind admissions policy for all undergraduate students worldwide, meeting 100% of demonstrated need with zero loans, and offers department-specific doctoral research funding, with terms stated in each offer.

scholarships_and_funding.name: President's PhD Scholarships
scholarships_and_funding.description: 50 awards for eligible PhD applicants worldwide. Covers full tuition fees, a £27,036 annual stipend for 2027-28, and £2,000 per year for consumables during the first three years; funding lasts 3.5 years.
scholarships_and_funding.eligibility: Applicants worldwide with outstanding academic and research potential must identify and obtain agreement from an Imperial supervisor, then select the scholarship in the PhD application. Department-specific conditions apply.
scholarships_and_funding.renewal: Funding lasts 3.5 years subject to award terms; £2,000 consumables support is for the first three years.
scholarships_and_funding.competition: 50 awards across Imperial; selection is competitive, and a supervisor agreement or eligible application does not guarantee an award.
scholarships_and_funding.course_application_deadline: Department and programme deadline; varies by PhD programme
steps: Contact an Imperial academic supervisor and obtain agreement to supervise.
Submit the PhD admission application through Imperial’s online application system.
Select President’s PhD Scholarship in the funding section of the additional questions.
Include the required two-page personal statement and department-specific application materials.
The department considers eligible applications; no standalone scholarship form is required.
documents: PhD application and research proposal
Transcripts and academic records
Two-page structured personal statement
Departmental statement and interview evidence as applicable

scholarships_and_funding.description: Funding terms, stipend amounts, and eligibility vary by individual Centre for Doctoral Training and studentship; check the relevant CDT page.

scholarships_and_funding.name: Dean’s Impact Scholarship
scholarships_and_funding.program_scope: Imperial Business School MSc and MBA programmes; confirm course participation
scholarships_and_funding.applicant_scope: Home and Overseas applicants entering an eligible Imperial Business School MSc or MBA programme
scholarships_and_funding.eligibility: New entrants with outstanding leadership potential, strong all-round applications and a demonstrated or prospective impact in business or society; confirm the eligible course.
scholarships_and_funding.renewal: The listed MSc and Full-Time MBA programmes are one-year courses; check the award offer for payment conditions.
scholarships_and_funding.competition: Competitive selection; the official scholarship page does not state a course-level award count.
scholarships_and_funding.course_application_deadline: Use the admission round published for the selected MSc or MBA course.
steps: Submit the eligible Imperial Business School MSc or MBA application.
After invitation, submit the scholarship assessment: written for MSc or video for MBA.
documents: Eligible course application and its required documents
Invited written assessment for MSc or video assessment for MBA
scholarships_and_funding.coverage: MSc: GBP 25,000; Full-Time MBA: up to 50% of tuition fees. An award is not guaranteed.
scholarships_and_funding.description: For new entrants across specified Imperial Business School master’s programmes. The 2027-28 award is £25,000 for MSc programmes and up to 50% of tuition fees for MBA programmes.

scholarships_and_funding.name: Imperial Bursary (Home Fee Status Only)
scholarships_and_funding.description: For Home undergraduate students starting in autumn 2026 or 2027 with household income below £70,000; award is £1,000–£5,000 per year by income. Eligible students qualify automatically.

scholarships_and_funding.name: Imperial Inspires Scholarship
scholarships_and_funding.program_scope: All undergraduate courses and selected postgraduate taught courses listed as participating; excludes postgraduate research
scholarships_and_funding.applicant_scope: International students eligible for the Overseas tuition fee rate
scholarships_and_funding.eligibility: Course must participate in Imperial Inspires and applicant must meet scholarship eligibility and course minimum entry requirements. At least 300 awards are offered for 2027 entry across Engineering, Natural Sciences, Medicine, and Imperial Business School.
scholarships_and_funding.coverage: £15,000 per year for each year of the course, towards tuition fees and living costs.
scholarships_and_funding.renewal: For awards longer than 11 months, eligibility is reviewed annually; award may be withdrawn for failure to meet academic expectations or other stated conditions.
scholarships_and_funding.competition: Highly competitive; Imperial says not all applicants will be successful. No course-level award count published.
scholarships_and_funding.course_application_deadline: Undergraduate UCAS deadline varies by course; many courses use the 2027-01-13 equal consideration deadline. Postgraduate taught deadline varies by course and admissions round.
scholarships_and_funding.deadline_timezone: Not published for the scholarship application
steps: Submit an undergraduate UCAS or postgraduate taught My Imperial application after applications open in September 2026.
Confirm that the chosen course participates in Imperial Inspires and that you meet its eligibility and minimum course requirements.
If eligible, wait for an invitation and submit the additional essay through the admissions i360 portal.
Check the award terms and conditions for the participating course and its current round.
documents: Course application and course-specific materials
Additional essay through i360 after invitation
Other required documents and exact scholarship criteria vary by participating course; not yet fully published

steps: Apply for admission to HBS.

steps: Submit the HKS master’s admission application by December 1, 2026 before accessing the financial-aid application.
Complete the HKS Financial Aid Application after applying for admission and before the admission decision; submit it by January 15, 2027 at 12 p.m. ET.
Complete household income and asset information and answer the award-eligibility questions in the financial-aid application.
Upload the general financial-aid essay (750 words maximum) describing public-service commitment, professional interests and aspirations, and how HKS will help meet those goals.
Upload any additional essay requested for an individual award; some research-center and CGS international fellowships require a separate application.
U.S. citizens, permanent residents, and eligible noncitizens are encouraged to submit FAFSA for federal student-loan eligibility.
documents: HKS Financial Aid Application with household income and asset information
General financial-aid essay, maximum 750 words
Additional award-specific essays or separate applications when required by the selected fellowship
FAFSA for U.S. citizens, permanent residents, or eligible noncitizens seeking federal student-loan eligibility (encouraged, not a universal fellowship requirement)
